questions.question: In a closed queueing network with $n\geq2$ circulating jobs and single-server first-come-first-served stations with exponential service times, a job arrives at station $i$. How are the other $n-1$ jobs it sees distributed over the stations?
options: Like the full network itself: the time-average law with $n$ jobs, as for Poisson arrivals.
Like a larger network: the time-average law with $n+1$ jobs, as the arrival adds itself.
Like a smaller network: the time-average law with $n-1$ jobs, as the job does not see itself.
As independent $M/M/1$ queues, one per station $j$, each with load $\mathrm{TH}_j(n)\mathbb{E}[S_j]$.

questions.question: For station $i$ of a closed network with $n$ jobs and single-server FCFS stations with exponential service, the arrival theorem gives $\mathbb{E}[J_i(n)]=\bigl(1+\mathbb{E}[L_i(n-1)]\bigr)\mathbb{E}[S_i]$. What does the term $1\cdot\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ account for?
options: The mean service time of the arriving job itself, received after the jobs it finds.
The remaining service of the job found in service, which $\mathbb{E}[L_i(n-1)]$ leaves out.
The arriving job added to the count, turning $\mathbb{E}[L_i(n-1)]$ into $\mathbb{E}[L_i(n)]$.
The service of one job that arrives later during the visit and is served first.

questions.question: Jobs arrive at station $i$ of a closed network with $n$ jobs and single-server FCFS stations with exponential service. Why can PASTA not be used to conclude that these arrivals see the time-average distribution of the $n$-job network?
options: PASTA fails in every network: even Poisson arrivals to a station inside a network never see time averages.
The arrivals at station $i$ are not a Poisson process: they occur at service completions elsewhere, at a state-dependent rate.
PASTA needs every station's load below 1, and in a closed network each station is busy all of the time.
PASTA does apply here; only the formula for the time per visit differs from the time-average one.

questions.question: In a closed network of single-server FCFS stations with exponential service, a job arrives at station $i$ while another job is in service there. Why does the arrival-theorem time per visit charge that job a full mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$?
options: Under FCFS the job in service has just started, so all of its service still remains.
The arrival theorem guarantees remaining service of mean $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ for any service distribution.
Little's law at station $i$ equates the mean remaining service with the mean service time.
Exponential service is memoryless, so the remaining service of the job in service has mean $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$.

questions.question: Mean value analysis computes the means of a closed network of single-server FCFS exponential stations population by population. To evaluate $\mathbb{E}[J_i(n)]$ with the arrival theorem, which quantity is needed besides $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$?
options: The mean $\mathbb{E}[L_i(n)]$ that station $i$ holds over time with the full population of $n$ jobs.
The throughput $\mathrm{TH}_1(n)$ at the reference station in the network with $n$ jobs.
The time-average mean $\mathbb{E}[L_i(n-1)]$ at station $i$ when the network has one job fewer.
The full time-average law of the numbers at all stations with $n$ jobs.

questions.question: In a closed queueing network of single-server first-come-first-served stations with exponential service times, station $i$ has $\mathbb{E}[S_i]=3$ minutes. The time-average mean number there is $\mathbb{E}[L_i(n)]=1.2$ with $n$ jobs and $\mathbb{E}[L_i(n-1)]=0.8$ with $n-1$ jobs. What is the mean time per visit $\mathbb{E}[J_i(n)]$ with $n$ jobs?
options: $2.4$ minutes
$5.4$ minutes
$6.6$ minutes
$8.4$ minutes

questions.question: A closed network holds a single job ($n=1$) and has two single-server FCFS stations with exponential service, $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=3$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=4$; station 2 has visit ratio $V_2=0.5$ visits per visit to station 1. The time-average mean at station 2 is $\mathbb{E}[L_2(1)]=0.4$. What is the mean time per visit $\mathbb{E}[J_2(1)]$?

A closed two-station cycle has single-server FCFS stations with exponential service of equal means and $n=4$ jobs. For such a cycle with $N$ jobs, the time-average number at station 1 is uniform on $\{0,1,\ldots,N\}$. What fraction of the jobs arriving at station 1 find all three other jobs there?

In a closed network with $n=3$ jobs and single-server FCFS stations with exponential service, station $i$ has mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S_i]=5$ minutes. A job arrives at station $i$ and finds the other two jobs there: one has already been in service for 3 minutes and one is waiting. What is the expected time from this arrival until the arriving job's own service at station $i$ ends?
options: $12$ minutes
$10$ minutes
$15$ minutes
$12.5$ minutes

questions.question: In a closed network with $n=4$ jobs, station $i$ is a single-server FCFS station with exponential service of mean $\mathbb{E}[S_i]=2$. A program reports the mean time per visit $\mathbb{E}[J_i(4)]=9$. Is this value possible?
options: Yes: up to four jobs can be ahead of an arrival, so the limit is $(1+4)\cdot2=10$.
No: an arrival finds at most three other jobs, so $\mathbb{E}[J_i(4)]\leq(1+3)\cdot2=8$.
Yes: as in an $M/M/1$ queue, the time per visit at the station has no upper limit.
No: only the job in service can be ahead of an arrival, so $\mathbb{E}[J_i(4)]\leq2\cdot2=4$.

questions.question: A closed two-station cycle has $n$ jobs and single-server stations with exponential service at rates $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$. Let $k$ be the number at station 1, with time-average law $p_n(k)$; each completion at station 2 sends a job to station 1. To which expression is the fraction of arrivals at station 1 that find $k$ jobs there proportional?
options: $p_n(k)$, for $k=0,\ldots,n$
$p_n(k-1)\,\mu_2\mathbf{1}\{k\geq1\}$
$p_n(k)\,\mu_2\mathbf{1}\{k\geq1\}$
$p_n(k)\,\mu_2\mathbf{1}\{k\leq n-1\}$

questions.question: Station $i$ of a closed network has two identical parallel servers with exponential service of mean $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, while every other station has one server. Why should $\bigl(1+\mathbb{E}[L_i(n-1)]\bigr)\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ not be used as the mean time per visit at station $i$?
options: It charges a full mean service per job found, as with one server; with two servers an arrival finding one job starts at once.
With two servers an arriving job sees only $n-2$ other jobs, so $\mathbb{E}[L_i(n-1)]$ must become $\mathbb{E}[L_i(n-2)]$.
Little's law fails at a station with two servers, so the mean times and mean numbers there no longer match.
With two servers the service times are no longer exponential, so the memoryless property cannot be used.

questions.question: A closed network has $m\geq3$ single-server FCFS stations with exponential service and $n\geq2$ jobs. A job arrives at station 1. Which statement about the number of other jobs it finds at station 2 is correct?
options: It follows the time-average law of $L_2$ in the $n$-job network, since the population shift applies only to station 1.
It equals $n-1$ minus the number found at station 1, since the other jobs are split between those two stations.
It follows the time-average law of $L_2$ in the $(n-1)$-job network, as part of the joint law of all other jobs.
It is independent of the number found at station 1, since the stations of a product-form network are independent.

questions.question: A closed two-station cycle has single-server FCFS stations with exponential service, $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=3$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=1$, and $n=3$ jobs. In the same network with 2 jobs the time-average mean at station 1 is $\mathbb{E}[L_1(2)]=21/13$. What is the mean time per visit $\mathbb{E}[J_2(3)]$ at station 2?

In a closed queueing network of single-server first-come-first-served stations with exponential service times, station 2 has $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=3$ and visit ratio $V_2=0.5$. Mean value analysis gives $\mathbb{E}[L_2(1)]=0.6$ with one job and throughput $\mathrm{TH}_1(2)=10/19$ at station 1 with two jobs. Using the arrival theorem and Little's law, what is $\mathbb{E}[L_2(2)]$?

A closed network has three single-server FCFS stations with exponential service, $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=2$, $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=2$, $\mathbb{E}[S_3]=6$, and visit ratios $V_1=1$, $V_2=0.5$, $V_3=0.5$. What is the mean time per visit $\mathbb{E}[J_3(2)]$ at station 3 when the network holds two jobs?

A closed network of single-server FCFS exponential stations has all $V_i>0$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_i]>0$. Its throughput satisfies $\mathrm{TH}_1(n)\leq n/\sum_iV_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, with equality for $n=1$. Why is this inequality strict for every $n\geq2$?
options: For $n\geq2$ the bottleneck bound $1/\max_iV_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ is always the smaller bound and takes over.
For $n\geq2$ a job found in service needs on average more than $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, which lengthens the cycle.
Arrivals find the other $n-1\geq1$ jobs somewhere, so $\sum_iV_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]\mathbb{E}[L_i(n-1)]>0$ lengthens the cycle.
For $n\geq2$ Little's law $n=\mathrm{TH}_1(n)\mathbb{E}[J(n)]$ holds only approximately, so equality is lost.

questions.question: In mean value analysis of a closed network with $n$ jobs, a student uses $\mathbb{E}[J_i(n)]=\bigl(1+\mathbb{E}[L_i(n)]\bigr)\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ at every station with the exact time-average means, then $\widehat{\mathrm{TH}}=n/\sum_iV_i\mathbb{E}[J_i(n)]$ and $\widehat{L}_i=V_i\widehat{\mathrm{TH}}\,\mathbb{E}[J_i(n)]$. Does the check $\sum_i\widehat{L}_i=n$ reveal the slip?
options: Yes: the slip lets jobs wait behind themselves, so $\sum_i\widehat{L}_i$ exceeds $n$.
No: $\sum_i\widehat{L}_i=\widehat{\mathrm{TH}}\sum_iV_i\mathbb{E}[J_i(n)]=n$, whatever times are used.
Yes: the inflated times lower the throughput, so $\sum_i\widehat{L}_i$ falls short of $n$.
No: the time-average means give the correct times here, so there is nothing to reveal.

questions.question: A closed two-station cycle has single-server FCFS stations with exponential service, $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=4$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=1$. Mean value analysis gives $\mathbb{E}[L_1(1)]=4/5$ and $\mathbb{E}[L_1(2)]=12/7$. A student computes $\mathbb{E}[J_1(2)]$ as $\bigl(1+\mathbb{E}[L_1(2)]\bigr)\mathbb{E}[S_1]$. Which statement about the student's value is correct?
options: It is $76/7\approx10.86$, the correct $\mathbb{E}[J_1(2)]$, since arrivals see time averages.
It is $48/7\approx6.86$, which lies below the correct $\mathbb{E}[J_1(2)]=36/5$.
It is $76/7\approx10.86$, exactly one mean service $\mathbb{E}[S_1]$ above the correct value.
It is $76/7\approx10.86$, which equals the correct $\mathbb{E}[J_1(3)]$ for three jobs.

questions.question: A closed cycle $1\to2\to3\to1$ has single-server FCFS stations with exponential service, $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=2$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=\mathbb{E}[S_3]=1$. The time-average law of the number at station 1 is $(3,4,4)/11$ on $\{0,1,2\}$ with 2 jobs and $(2,3,4,4)/13$ on $\{0,1,2,3\}$ with 3 jobs. What is $\mathbb{E}[J_1(3)]$ with 3 jobs?
